name: Drought
value: Sudan, eastern Australia dry; no famine call
summary: El Niño dryness hits Sudan's farm belt and eastern Australia; no new famine declaration or exporter harvest failure
state: Sudan's July–September rains were the lowest in more than three decades, with some Gedaref and North Kordofan farmers expecting a quarter of normal yields; the IPC warned on 12 Oct that famine risk is growing in conflict areas, but no new famine has been declared (Reuters via TimesLIVE, 23 Oct). In eastern Australia, rainfall was no more than 25% of normal between 22 Aug and 20 Sep (DTN). Severe drought in major crop regions keeps this at Watch; no drought-driven famine or major exporter harvest failure was found as of 12 Nov.
for_you: Farmers in Sudan and eastern Australia and people in Sudan's conflict areas who rely on local harvests are most exposed. Food prices tend to follow poor harvests with a lag of some months.
rubric_hit: Watch: severe drought in a major crop region (Sudan's lowest Jul–Sep rains in 30+ years; eastern Australia ≤25% of normal rain)

sources.title: TimesLIVE (Reuters) — New famine risk haunts war-torn Sudan with El Niño-driven drought
DTN — El Niño-related dryness to reduce wheat

why: Drought slowly destroys harvests, hydropower and river shipping, and drives famine and migration.
drivers: Rainfall deficits, heat, ENSO, groundwater depletion.

rubric.alert: Drought driving famine conditions, a major exporter's harvest failure, or monsoon failure across a major breadbasket.
rubric.watch: Severe drought in a major crop region, a major river at record low, or a monsoon running more than 20% below normal.
rubric.normal: No major breadbasket in severe drought.
